text.p: Bear Stearns on Friday said it lowered its rating on Mexican builder Consortio ARA to neutral from attractive.

"Continued outperformance could be challenging after the stock's 70 percent climb since the September 1996 IPO," analysts Sobani Warner and Daniel Altman said, adding they have high expectations for earnings growth.

The analysts said Mexico is entering into a weaker housing pricing environment in the low-income segment, which could limit up-side potential for the company. Residential sales also remain depressed because of low private sector mortgage lending, they said.
"For Q1 1997, we expect a decent performance, but it is not likely to be as spectacular as the previous quarter," the analysts said in a report.
Bear Stearns estimate for earnings per Mexican shares in 1997 is 1.55 pesos, and 2.30 pesos for 1998.
Mexican shares closed trading on Thursday at 28.20 pesos per share.
